title: Serenade No. 13 in G major, “Eine kleine Nachtmusik”
hook: Mozart’s most famous serenade, finished in the summer he was writing Don Giovanni.

painting.title: Mezzetin
painting.collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
painting.pairingNote: A comedian of the Italian theatre sings to his guitar in a garden; a serenade, the evening music that Mozart’s title, “a little night music”, names.

facts: Mozart entered the work in his own catalogue of compositions on 10 August 1787, in Vienna. He was in the middle of writing his opera *Don Giovanni* at the time.

Nobody knows why he wrote it, who asked for it, or whether it was ever played in his lifetime. Most of his serenades were commissions, so it may have been one whose first performance simply went unrecorded.

The famous name comes from that catalogue entry, which begins “Eine kleine Nacht-Musick”. It means “a little night music”, but Mozart was probably just noting that he had finished “a little serenade”, not giving it a title.

The same entry lists five movements, with a minuet and trio after the opening Allegro. That movement is lost; no one knows who removed it. The serenade was published only around 1827, long after Mozart’s death, when his widow Constanze sold it to a publisher with a bundle of his manuscripts.
It is written for five string players (two violins, viola, cello and double bass) but is usually played, as here, by a string orchestra.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a brisk, sunny opening (I), a gentle song with a darker middle (II), a firm little dance (III), a quick, playful finale (IV).

movements.heading: Allegro
movements.summary: The strings shoot up the notes of the home chord together, and the whole movement grows from that bright, confident gesture. It is a compact [[sonata-form|sonata form]]: two contrasting themes, a short development, and a return. Everything is clear and in proportion, and nothing outstays its welcome.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1, the call
mainIdeas.description: all the strings together, loud, leaping up the notes of the G major chord, then a quicker answer.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a soft, graceful phrase that falls gently, with little turns, in D major.

mainIdeas.name: The chatter
mainIdeas.description: a small tune on quick repeated notes with a trill, broken off by loud chords.

stops.hear: All the strings together, loud: a call that leaps up the notes of a chord, answered by a quicker, busier figure
Suddenly quiet: a smooth phrase in long notes, then light, dancing steps
The violins shiver on fast repeated notes and climb, getting louder
stops.happening: The bridge to a new key

stops.hear: A soft, graceful tune that falls step by step, with little turns
A chattering little tune on repeated notes, with a trill each time, interrupted by loud chords
The opening call again, exactly as before
The call returns in a new key; then the chattering tune wanders quietly through darker keys and climbs back up on a long scale
stops.happening: The [[development|development]], only about twenty bars long

stops.hear: The opening call, back in G major
The graceful falling tune again, now in the home key

stops.label: Last 15 seconds
stops.hear: Loud repeated chords, with the call broken into short pieces

notice: The first two bars are a single chord, spread out and climbing. Listen to how often the movement comes back to that shape.
Compare the two halves. The development is tiny; the movement is about clear statements, not long arguments.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Karajan recorded the serenade with the strings of the Berlin Philharmonic, a fuller sound than five solo players would make. He repeats the exposition but not the second half. On the Spotify album the serenade is tracks 1–4, followed by the *Serenata notturna*, K. 239, and the Divertimento in B-flat, K. 287.

movements.heading: Romance: Andante
movements.summary: A slow, tender song. A [[romance|romance]] was a gentle, song-like piece, and this one is a [[rondo|rondo]]: its main tune keeps coming back between two contrasting passages. The second of them turns to the minor and becomes restless, before the calm tune returns.

mainIdeas.name: The romance tune
mainIdeas.description: a gentle melody in the first violins that always starts a little before the main beat, like a dance step.

mainIdeas.name: The light episode
mainIdeas.description: quick, airy notes in the first violins over even, repeated chords.

mainIdeas.name: The minor episode
mainIdeas.description: short, anxious phrases with little turns, over a fast, nervous murmur in the second violins and violas.

stops.hear: Soft and singing: the first violins play a gentle tune that begins just before the beat
stops.happening: The romance tune (A), first half, played twice

stops.hear: A second phrase with small sighs, then the tune again; also repeated
Lighter: quick, airy notes in the first violins over even, repeated chords
stops.happening: The first episode (B), in C major

stops.hear: The opening tune again, but only its first half
The music turns to the minor: short, anxious phrases above a fast, restless murmur in the middle strings
stops.happening: The second episode (C), in C minor

stops.hear: Calm returns with the opening tune, complete
Quiet closing phrases; the melody sinks lower and comes to rest

notice: In the minor episode, listen below the tune. The second violins and violas keep up a fast, even murmur that gives the passage its unease.

movements.heading: Menuetto: Allegretto
movements.summary: A short, firm [[minuet|minuet]], the courtly dance in three beats, with a softer [[trio|trio]] in the middle. The minuet stamps; the trio sings quietly.

mainIdeas.name: The minuet
mainIdeas.description: loud, clear steps up the scale, in a strong three-beat rhythm.

mainIdeas.name: The trio
mainIdeas.description: a smooth, soft melody in D major, marked *sotto voce* (“under the voice”).

stops.hear: Loud, firm steps in a three-beat dance rhythm, all the strings together
stops.happening: The minuet, G major, first half (repeated)

stops.hear: The dance continues, still loud and clear; this half is repeated too
Very soft and smooth: the first violins sing a flowing tune over a quiet accompaniment
The firm minuet comes back
stops.happening: The minuet again, this time without repeats

notice: The trio is not slower, only softer and smoother. Listen to how much the mood changes with the same three-beat pulse.

movements.heading: Rondo: Allegro
movements.summary: A quick, high-spirited finale. Mozart calls it a rondo, but it is built more like a [[sonata-form|sonata form]], with two themes, a development and a return. Its main tune is a cheeky little upbeat followed by repeated notes.

mainIdeas.name: The main tune
mainIdeas.description: three quick rising notes, then repeated notes on one pitch; quiet and light.

mainIdeas.name: The loud answer
mainIdeas.description: the whole group, firm and bright.

stops.hear: Quiet and quick: three rising notes, then the same note repeated; the phrase is played twice
Loud and bright: the whole group answers with a firm, busy passage
Quiet again: the rising notes and repeated notes, now in a new key
stops.happening: The second group of themes, in D major

stops.hear: A sudden change of colour: the main tune’s rising notes in a distant key
A loud cadence phrase, but in the minor
stops.happening: The return begins with only the last bars of the main tune, in G minor

stops.hear: The quiet tune in G major again
stops.happening: The second group, now in the home key

stops.label: Last 20 seconds
stops.hear: The rising notes climb again and again, then loud final chords

notice: Listen for the jump into E-flat major near the middle. It lasts only a few seconds, but it is the one surprise in a very sunny movement.

threads.title: A serenade, not a symphony
threads.body: Light music for an evening, written for five players. The ideas are short and clear, and every movement is easy to follow on a first hearing.

threads.title: The missing minuet
threads.body: Mozart planned a second minuet after the first movement. Without it, the work has the four-movement shape of a small symphony.

threads.title: Hidden shadows
threads.body: The minor-key middle of the Romance and the brief E-flat surprise of the finale are the only clouds, and both pass quickly.
